title: The Accessibility Guy Podcast
author: Shawn Jordison
description:
Where accessibility meets real-world application.

Hosted by Shawn Jordison, digital accessibility consultant, trainer, and advocate, this show dives deep into the world of inclusive design, accessible technology, and the policies shaping our digital spaces. Each episode features candid conversations with experts, advocates, and everyday changemakers working to make documents, websites, videos, and software usable for everyone, including people with disabilities.

We explore accessibility from every angle:

Laws & Standards – Section 508, WCAG, ADA, AODA, Colorado HB21-1110, PDF/UA, and other regulations that shape compliance.

Practical Solutions – Tools, workflows, and strategies for creating accessible PDFs, Microsoft Office documents, and multimedia content.

Assistive Technology – How screen readers, captions, keyboard navigation, and other tools transform digital access.

Real-World Stories – Insights from educators, government officials, designers, developers, and advocates who are making a tangible impact.

Listeners can expect a mix of professional insights and practical takeaways. If you work in higher education, government, K–12 districts, nonprofits, or small business, you’ll find actionable advice that’s clear, simple, and ready to implement.

Every guest answers our signature questions, giving you a personal look at how accessibility impacts their work and life. From small victories to big systemic changes, you’ll hear stories that inspire action and highlight why accessibility matters—not just as a legal requirement, but as a human right.

Shawn’s own background spans years of helping organizations meet accessibility standards, remediate documents, train staff, and navigate complex legal requirements. Through this podcast, his mission is simple: make accessibility less overwhelming and more achievable for everyone.

Expect episodes that break down technical concepts without jargon, uncover creative problem-solving approaches, and share resources you can put to use right away.

What you’ll get from this podcast:

Clear, plain-language explanations of accessibility standards

Step-by-step tips for document and web accessibility

Interviews with leaders in the accessibility space

Stories from people directly impacted by accessibility barriers—and solutions that worked

Regular discussions on new laws, technology updates, and best practices

If you’re ready to learn, be inspired, and take concrete steps toward making your content, technology, and workplace accessible, this is your space.

Subscribe now to The Accessibility Guy Podcast, because accessibility is more than compliance. It’s about connection, equity, and building a world where everyone can participate fully.

The advantage may shift from simply knowing information to knowing how to apply judgment, context, creativity, strategy, and human insight alongside intelligent machines.Whether you're learning AI for the first time, developing your career, building a business, teaching others, or preparing for the future of work, The AI Learning Advantage provides practical insights designed to help you stay ahead of technological change.This is not simply a podcast about artificial intelligence.It is a podcast about how humans can become more capable in an AI-powered world.

  • leadership psychology and human behavior in organizations

You’ll get clear frameworks you can apply immediately—especially The APEXIA CALM Framework: Clarity, Accountability, Language, Modeling. When leadership gets noisy, we go CALM.


Expect calm, practical teaching, a little humor (sometimes the workplace deserves it), and occasional deep dives into academic research—without turning the show into a lecture.


If you care about becoming the kind of leader people trust—and the kind of workplace people don’t need to recover from—this is for you.


Listeners can expect:


  • practical frameworks (clear enough to remember, strong enough to run a team on)
  • leadership psychology + human behavior explained plainly

description:

These images of strength and resilience emerge from the narration of Shantoo Gurnani - a narration that informs us about educational choices women made in the thirties and forties and the careers in science opening out for women in the early half of the century.

The Profound Parent Podcast

Parenting a child with profound autism and complex support needs requires a depth of knowledge, courage, and advocacy that few people truly understand. The Profound Parent Podcast is for parents raising children with high support needs—including nonspeaking or unreliably speaking children—and navigating a world that doesn't always know how to see the whole person.

A Profound Parent isn't defined by a diagnosis. They're defined by the depth of knowledge, resilience, and fierce advocacy they develop along the way.

This podcast explores what it really means to raise a child with profound autism, complex support needs, and significant communication challenges while holding two truths at once: a child can have profound, lifelong support needs and be thoughtful, intelligent, curious, and capable of learning.

Difficulty demonstrating ability is not the same as an absence of ability.

Each episode brings you real stories, practical tools, honest conversations, and mindset shifts for navigating communication, advocacy, education, AAC, daily life, and the complicated realities of high-support-needs parenting. We talk about what it means to presume competence, support communication, understand behavior, and advocate fiercely—even when the world underestimates your child.

Because understanding profound support needs should never mean underestimating the person.

The Profound Parent Podcast: Understanding profound needs without underestimating the person.

author: Linh Podetti & Jennifer Cao

Hosted by Linh Podetti and Jennifer Cao, both of whom have lived the journey of single motherhood, this podcast offers real stories, practical wisdom, and empowering conversations. title: The Receiving Edge
author: Sarah Blackah
description:
Life doesn't always unfold the way we imagined.
You might be standing at the edge of a new beginning, grieving something that has ended, or carrying both at once, living in the space between what was and who you're becoming. That space can feel lonely, and it's where most of real life happens.
Sarah Blackah calls it the Receiving Edge. It's where our deepest desires meet God's invitation, the place where longing, obedience, hope and surrender all live at once, and where even the hardest seasons can become a doorway to something good and true and beautiful.
The Receiving Edge is a podcast about learning to trust God with what matters most while the story is still unfolding. Through long-form conversations, powerful testimonies and honest solo reflections, Sarah explores how ordinary people kept trusting God when life went differently than they planned. Love and marriage. Motherhood, fertility and family. Calling, creativity and stewardship. Health and healing. Provision, wealth and legacy. Community and belonging. Grief.
Underneath all of it sits one question: can God be trusted with the deepest desires of our hearts?
Sarah is hosting this from the middle of her own story. For more than a decade she built global communities, led teams and created multiple seven figures in health and wellness. Then a life quake took apart the certainty she had built her life on, and sent her back to the questions she had spent years outrunning. What is true? What am I building my life on? Why do I feel so far from the thing that matters most to me? She's still in it, and that's exactly where these conversations happen.
Whether you're longing for a relationship, waiting for a baby, navigating a career pivot, rebuilding after loss, chasing a dream, or quietly sensing that God is inviting you into something deeper, you're welcome here. This is a place to put down the performance, embrace being human, and take the next faithful step while the story is still unfolding.
Every episode ends with the same question: what Receiving Edge are you standing at right now, and what's the next faithful step you're being invited to take?
New episodes weekly. 
A 3V Media Productions podcast.
Follow along on Instagram @Sarahblackah

The season where we're raising kids while rediscovering ourselves, watching our bodies change, questioning things we thought we'd already figured out, navigating marriage and friendships, caring for aging parents, building careers, setting boundaries, losing people, and occasionally wondering when exactly we're supposed to start feeling like the grown-ups in the room.

title: Brickhouse Investing Tips
author: brickhouse
description: In the world of traditional finance, the standard doctrine passed down through generations of financial advisors, academic textbooks, and institutional practices is the fundamental trade-off between risk and return. This classic framework asserts that if you want higher returns, you must accept proportionally higher risk. If you desire safety, you must settle for low yields.However, many of the world's most successful investors—from Warren Buffett and Mohnish Pabrai to Paul Tudor Jones and Nassim Nicholas Taleb—do not operate on this linear spectrum. Instead, they seek out asymmetric opportunities: investments where the potential upside drastically outweighs the potential downside.

title: The Seasonal Edit
author: Jade Boyd
description:
The Seasonal Edit is a planning, productivity, and intentional living podcast for women who want to feel less overwhelmed by their lives—and more present for them.
Hosted by Jade Boyd, MBA, productivity expert and planner creator, The Seasonal Edit takes a practical, realistic approach to getting your life in order without turning it into one endless self-improvement project.
Because the goal isn't to squeeze more into your days. It's to get better at deciding what matters, create simple systems that make everyday life easier, and make room for the things you actually want to enjoy.
Each episode blends thoughtful perspective with practical, actionable strategies for planning, organization, routines, time management, productivity, goal setting, simple living, and managing a home and family. You'll learn how to organize your weeks, create routines that actually stick, simplify your home, manage the mental load, make progress on meaningful goals, and use your limited time and energy more intentionally.
And unlike productivity advice that assumes every week of your life should look the same, The Seasonal Edit is built around a different idea: your systems should change when your season does.
Your capacity changes. Your priorities change. Your family changes. Your energy changes. Even the literal seasons affect the rhythms of your home and life. Instead of forcing yourself into a rigid routine year-round, you'll learn how to regularly edit what's on your plate and build rhythms that support the life you're actually living right now.
This podcast is for you if you've ever wondered: How do I create routines that don't just look good on paper but actually work for real life? How do I stay organized when I'm managing a million little things that don't fit in tidy boxes? How can I make time for my goals, creative work, side hustle, or hobbies when my free time is limited? How do I simplify and declutter my home without making it another overwhelming project? How can I be productive without constantly feeling rushed or behind? What should I focus on first when everything feels important? How do I stop trying to do everything—and still make meaningful progress?
Whether you're resetting your weekly routine, organizing your home, planning your next season, trying to get dinner on the table with less stress, or figuring out what deserves your attention in a particularly full season of life, you'll leave these episodes with ideas you can actually use.
No impossible morning routines. No pressure to optimize every minute. No recycled list of “10 habits successful women do before 5 a.m.” Just thoughtful, practical strategies for doing less—but doing what matters better.
Because a well-planned life shouldn't just look productive on paper. It should feel good in your everyday life. Start with the season you're in now by downloading Jade's free Seasonal Living Guide at jadeboyd.co/season.

description:
We Didn’t Plan for This Podcast
Life rarely goes according to plan. People definitely don’t.

We Didn’t Plan for This is about the stuff nobody prepares you for — grief, friendship, family, relationships, getting older, starting over, changing your mind, and figuring out who you are when life looks nothing like you thought it would.

Some episodes go deep. Some go completely off the rails. Most do a little of both.

And then there’s People Be Peopling — our slightly less serious investigation into the weird, hilarious, wildly relatable things humans do. Why do we tell our hairdresser our entire life story? Why do strangers confess their deepest secrets on airplanes? Why do group texts become emotional war zones? And why does every family have that one person?

Because sometimes life is heartbreaking. Sometimes people are ridiculous. And sometimes the best way through all of it is to sit down with someone you love and say, “Okay…what the hell was that?”

Real stories. Real conversations. Very little pretending we have it all figured out.

We didn’t plan for this. But here we are.

In Case of Emergency, Press Play: Meditation for real life — especially when real life is being a lot.


In Case of Emergency, Press Play is a collection of short, approachable guided meditations for anxiety, stress, grief, overthinking, self-doubt, sleep, letting go, finding focus, and those days when your nervous system seems to have its own agenda.


No perfect meditation practice required. No need to clear your mind, sit perfectly still, or suddenly become a person who has everything figured out.

Just press play.


Each episode gives you a few minutes to breathe, ground, reset, and reconnect with yourself — whether you’re starting your morning, lying awake at night, sitting in your car before walking into work, navigating something hard, or simply needing a minute.

Welcome to “Democracy Bytes,” where we deeply explore the intricate relationship between technology and democracy. I’m Alice, your guide on this journey into our increasingly digital democracy.
Throughout this series, we’ll investigate pivotal topics and their multifaceted impacts on our democratic society. We’ll explore the effects of AI and social media on democracy, as well as the interesting dynamics of how technology affects democracy. 
In each episode, we'll be joined by an array of policymakers, experts, and ordinary people, each offering rich insights and diverse perspectives on the ethical, regulatory, and societal ramifications of technology, AI and social media. Our discussions will tackle controversial and complex topics, from potential biases in AI and the need for content regulation to the ethical dilemmas arising from advancements in artificial intelligence.
As we uncover the impacts of AI and social media on our societal norms, individual rights, and the very fabric of democracy, we hope to enlighten you with insightful and interesting perspectives on the many new ways to participate in the democratic process.

title: Audiobooks
author: guy
description:
Audiobooks are the modern bridge between the ancient art of storytelling and the fast-paced rhythm of contemporary life. They transform the written word into a living, breathing experience through the power of voice. Whether narrated by the author or a skilled performer, audiobooks carry the emotion, tone, and rhythm that can often be lost on the printed page.
They invite listeners into worlds of imagination, knowledge, and emotion—through headphones, speakers, or car stereos—turning any moment into an opportunity to learn, feel, or escape. In essence, audiobooks are literature in motion. They allow stories to accompany us as we walk, drive, or rest. They are for the commuter seeking inspiration, the traveler longing for company, or the lifelong learner expanding their mind without the constraint of a page.
The beauty of an audiobook lies not only in its content but in the intimacy of its delivery. The human voice adds warmth, depth, and subtlety—transforming reading into listening, and listening into an immersive, personal journey. In a world where time feels scarce, audiobooks offer a way to reclaim it. They make knowledge and art more accessible, inclusive, and dynamic. They remind us that storytelling began with the voice—and through audiobooks, the voice continues to shape how we connect with stories today.
RSSVERIFY

title: 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐑𝐎𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐃𝐄𝐍
author: Ophelia The Mystic
description:
The Rose of Eden is a journey into the mysteries of the Rose.
Through the symbolism of the rose, the wisdom of the Divine Feminine, and the stories of the women who carried sacred knowledge, we explore what it means to return to the feminine as something powerful, mystical, embodied, and whole.
Each episode weaves together Rose Lineage teachings, rose symbolism and healing, female archetypes, Christian mysticism, mythology, and ancient spiritual traditions—from Mary Magdalene, Aphrodite, Eve, Sophia, and Yeshua to the deeper mysteries hidden within their stories.
This is a space for questioning what we were taught, reclaiming what was forgotten, and discovering the sacred feminine through the language of the rose.
The Rose of Eden is an invitation to remember:
🌹 You were never meant to bloom without depth.
🌹 The feminine is not something to fear—it is something to remember.
🌹 And sometimes, the oldest mysteries are hidden in plain sight.
Welcome to the Rose of Eden.

title: Next in Transportation
author: Autodesk
description: Next in Transportation is a brand-new industry podcast exploring how infrastructure delivery is evolving across the networks that keep society moving—from roads, rail, ports, and airports to water, energy, and data. Examining both the status quo and what’s on the horizon, it showcases expert insights that reveal how approaches are applied in practice, why challenges persist, and what obstacles block progress.

title: UAA women’s basketball talk show
author: Bauer Michael
description: Get ready for this upcoming basketball season I’ll be doing deep dive into each games and where we stand in the rankings, and conference standings and so much more.

title: Femme Photon | Forbidden Inheritance
author: Femme Photon
description: Drop the good girl act. You've been performing empathy like it makes you a deep, moral good girl who automatically deserves her prizes. It doesn't, angel. It makes you devastatingly easy to manage. Femme Photon is your vault-locked salon of forbidden, scholar-level feminine intel. Without this, your brilliance rots into the ordinary. Walk into any room already holding a scandalous female advantage. Cash out on your intellect, discipline, beauty, and sex until resources orient around you. For the women too turned on to go back. Private erotic intel, behind closed doors. Claim your Forbidden Inheritance → https://www.femmephoton.com

title: Indie Film Lodge
author: Indie Film Lodge
description:
A deep dive into the nuts and bolts of independent filmmaking with hosts (and indie filmmakers) Robb Padgett and Matt Jackson.

Each week we'll speak to a different filmmaker about the trials and tribulations of making their film and do a dig in on a specific topic that they learned while making the film.

title: Healing From God
author: Eileen Lawson
description: What God’s Word Says about His Available Healing for Your Body - How to take God’s Medicine.

title: The Bronco Liam SHow
author: Liam Decker
description: This is a sports show so that everyone can listen to the top news going around within the sports world.

title: The ShameFree Life
author: Ketih H.
description: Join certified addiction recovery coach Keith as he helps men break free from pornography addiction through authentic connection with God and others—because the opposite of addiction isn't sobriety, it's connection. Discover lasting freedom through grace, neuroscience, and spirit-filled truth instead of shame and willpower.

title: How'd You Start
author: Nick Harrison
description: How’d You Start? is a behind-the-scenes look at the real journeys of entrepreneurs who took the leap to build something of their own. Whether you’re dreaming about quitting your 9-5, growing a side hustle, or already deep in the trenches of building your business, this show is for you.

title: Unmarked Trail
author: Don Hornsby
description: Unmarked Trail is a podcast for curious people who want to approach the Bible with fresh eyes. No church background required. No pressure to arrive with all the answers. We’ll learn how to read the Bible carefully, honestly, and in context, and then put those tools into practice by reading books of the Bible together. Hosted by Don Hornsby.

title: I Have Questions with Denver Health
author: Denver Health
description: You've just accessed the wisdom and expertise of Colorado's most trusted healthcare system. Ask Denver Health experts the questions you've always wanted to ask (or the ones you've been too embarrassed or too afraid to ask during your visits). We'll find the right expert to answer your questions and sit them down to hear their honest answers—no lab coats, no stethoscopes, no exam rooms.

title: Historia Podcast: Business Simulation Podcast
author: Andrew Callon
description:
Have you ever wanted to hear business simulations? Listen to a fictional company collapse? A man's entire life crumble before you?
Historia Podcast gives you this pleasure, allowing you to passively learn from business mistakes and learn about business traps that companies can fall for, from small coffee shops to massive cornerstone corporations.
Follow and listen as I release these fictional companies' risings and downfalls and enjoy!

title: The Seerah Podcast
author: Shaykh AbdulNasir Jangda
description:
Welcome to Seerah Pearls, which aims to highlight some tantalising learning points from each episode of the Seerah- Life of the Prophet (sallallahu alayhi wasallam).

This series hopes to be different from dry, factual studies, or ‘superhero-tales’, which we may feel we cannot ever aspire to: it aims to humanise the Prophet Muhammad (sallallahu alayhi wasallam)  and provide eternal practical lessons for every-day life, as well as engender love for the best of humankind. How can you possibly love someone you do not know?

title: Beyond the Crown with Lexy Romano
author: Lexy
description:
Hosted by Lexy Romano, Mrs. Arizona 2026, Beyond the Crown follows Lexy’s journey to becoming Mrs. Arizona and the people who have helped her along the way.


Through personal stories and conversations with special guests, Lexy shares the experiences that shaped her path to the crown and introduces listeners to the people, businesses, organizations, and sponsors who have supported her journey.

From pageantry and personal growth to community, philanthropy, and life as Mrs. Arizona, Beyond the Crown offers a look at Lexy’s story and the relationships and experiences that have made it possible.


Follow Lexy’s journey as Mrs. Arizona 2026 on Instagram:

@lexyromano_
@mrsarizonaamericapageant


Beyond the Crown is produced by TurnKey Media.

title: Common Sense Optional Podcast
author: Common Sense Optional
description:
Welcome to Common Sense Optional with Diana and Scott, we believe the best conversations happen when people are free to ask questions, change their minds, laugh at themselves, and appreciate different perspectives.
Common Sense Optional brings people together through honest, humorous conversations about current events, pop culture, and the beautifully confusing experience of midlife. Through the perspectives of two friends from different backgrounds, we encourage curiosity over certainty, laughter over outrage, and meaningful conversation over division. Our goal is simple: to create a space to hang out where listeners can take a break from the noise, think out loud, and leave feeling a little lighter, a little wiser, and a little less alone.
Our hope is that every episode feels like time spent with friends who make you laugh, make you think, and remind you that it’s okay to have questions. Around here common sense isn’t a requirement. Kindness, curiosity, and a good sense of humor are required and they always have a seat at our table.

title: Damaged Goods with Andrea Abbate
author: Andrea Abbate and Alex Duffant
description: DO YOU HAVE HERPES!? Have you been molested?! HIT?!?! Do you have a restraining order?? THIS PODCAST IS FOR YOU! Stand-up comedian Andrea Abbate hosts this darkly funny podcast that blends unapologetic humor with a touch of self-help. Joined by fellow stand-up comedian Alex Duffant, Andrea brings on her friends to talk life’s darkest moments and how they persevered.

title: The Care & Support Pod By HomeSuite
author: HomeSuite
description:
The Care & Support Pod is where care and support professionals have the real conversations the sector needs.

We go beyond the polished statements and safe answers—tackling the issues that affect quality, leadership, workforce, compliance, commissioning, technology and outcomes for the people services support.

From children’s homes and supported accommodation to supported living, fostering, domiciliary care, specialist provision and beyond, we speak to the people doing the work, challenging the system and saying what needs to be said.

Presented by HomeSuite.

title: The EBITDA Gap
author: Afrozy Ara
description:
Most organizations have adopted AI. Few can show what it did to the bottom line. The EBITDA Gap is a podcast hosted by Afrozy Ara, Founder and CEO of LuminaData, where business and finance leaders get candid about the real story behind AI transformation, what worked, what didn't, and what it actually took to move a number that shows up on the income statement.
Each episode is less interview, more conversation. No hype, no vague productivity wins — just honest discussion about the decisions, the workflows, and the outcomes that matter to anyone serious about making AI pay off.
Backed by Techstars and Berkeley SkyDeck, LuminaData helps organizations close the gap between AI adoption and measurable EBITDA impact. This podcast is the conversation that goes alongside that work.
New episodes drop regularly. Subscribe wherever you listen to podcasts.

title: Take a Seat with Sara
author: Sara Fredericks
description: Take a Seat with Sara

title: Signals From The Stack
author: Kim and Stefan
description:
Your professional reading stack is already too big. We’re here to help!

"Signals from the Stack" is a book-club-style podcast where two educators read, discuss, question, and rate books about education, technology, learning, and the ideas shaping schools. We dig past the headlines, wrestle with the research, disagree when necessary, and try to figure out what’s actually worth your time.

Expect thoughtful conversation, questionable jokes, strong opinions held loosely, and plenty of definitely real episode sponsors.

Listen along and decide which books deserve a spot at the top of your stack and which ones can stay there collecting dust.

title: The Compost Podcast
author: Compostable.ca
description:
The Compost Podcast explores everything compost — from food waste, organics recycling and composting technology to soil health, climate change, circular economy solutions and the future of sustainable waste management.
Presented by Compostable.ca, the podcast brings together composting industry experts, researchers, innovators, businesses and community leaders to explore the science, challenges, policies, technologies and real-world solutions shaping composting in Canada and around the world.
Each episode turns research and industry knowledge into practical, balanced conversations about how we can keep organic waste out of landfills, return valuable nutrients to the soil, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and build more resilient communities.
Whether you work in the composting and organics industry, manage food or organic waste, develop sustainability initiatives, or simply want to understand how compost can be part of the climate solution, **The Compost Podcast. is a place to learn, exchange ideas and discover what’s working.
Better waste. Healthier soil. More resilient communities. It all comes back to compost.

title: Hugo Atelier
author: Jonathan Hugo
description:
Hugo Atelier is a podcast for creatives who've hit their goals but still feel like something's missing. Hosted by filmmaker and brand strategist Jonathan Hugo, this show was created for the in-between moments - when old goals no longer fit and the question becomes, "what now?"
Each episode explores the mindset shifts, personal growth, and real-life pivots that help creative entrepreneurs break through both in business and life. With a grounded, honest voice, Jonathan challenges the idea that success is about doing more, and instead invites listeners to see differently, create from overflow, and live with lasting impact.

title: After the Sauna
author: Dan, Dave, Liam, and Ryan
description:
The steam has cleared, the gossip has started and absolutely nothing is off limits.
Join us each week as we dive into hilarious stories, unfiltered opinions, pop culture, dating disasters, LGBTQ+ life, gaming, superheroes, anime, and whatever else is living rent-free in our heads. Expect plenty of laughs, a bit of chaos, the occasional overshare, and enough hot takes to keep things interesting.
Whether you're here for the banter, the tea, or just want to feel like you're hanging out with mates after a long day, pull up a bench and join the conversation.

title: (PodBean) Hash It Out
author: Woodlawn Baptist Church
description: (PodBean) Hash It Out

title: Proud of You, Babe
author: Samantha Steinhage
description:
In these episodes we’re sharing conversations that connect, stories that inspire, and creating space for people to be seen, heard, and celebrated (oh yea. And laugh until we cry) because sometimes we all just need someone to say...
I’m proud of you, babe.

title: In the Game
author: Ghostbeane
description: Peeling back the onion and seeing what's really behind a gamer. We talk about the importance of games and the foundation they have built in the lives of everyone around them. Games aren't just pixels on a screen they are gateways to communities and worlds outside of our own

title: Beyond The Silence: Overthinking, Oversharing And ‘Adulting’
author: Lindy Lou
description:
Welcome to Beyond the Silence! It's the podcast for anyone who thought adults had it all figured out… and then became one. 
Hosted by Lindy Lou, expect honest chats about overthinking, confidence, self-worth, finding your voice and the general chaos of being a grown-up with no instruction manual. No perfection, no pretending, just real talk and laughs!
If you’ve ever looked around and wondered how everyone else is doing it? welcome, because here, you’ve found your people!
Welcome, Unsupervised Adults, I’m so glad you’re here!

title: AK’s Freequency
author: AK
description: Religious all about my journey, my life’s journey

title: Tomorrow Will Be A Better Day
author: Oskar Knoblauch and Jyll Harthun
description: “Tomorrow will be a better day”, is what my mother said to me and my siblings almost every day while living through the nightmare of the Holocaust. The day after we escaped, I made the decision to start a new life and choose happiness. Please join my granddaughter and host, Jyll, as she surprises me with requests to tell my stories of love, hope, curiosity, and conviction from life after the war that she and other family and friends would like to hear again. I am thrilled to share these stories with you for the first time. Welcome to the family! Shalom!

title: Futebol & Football with Tim Vickery & Henry Winter
author: Mark Machado
description: Tim Vickery and Henry Winter talk Futebal & Football

title: Utility Leaders with James Foden
author: Telos Co
description:
A podcast where great minds come together to discuss their careers, the evolution and sustainability of the Water Sector.
Inspired and hosted by James Foden a seasoned engineering and executive search consultant (Recruitment Consultant) Utility Leaders is a space for connection and collaboration, it is a place to share ideas and thoughts that lead to inspiring conversations. 
Utility Leaders is a space where industry professionals and thought leaders can share their journey to engage, educate and inspire the next generation of water sector professionals.

title: This Is Not Advice
author: Kareem and Shannon
description:
This Is Not Advice is a fun, honest, and unfiltered podcast hosted by Kareem and Shannon, a married couple sharing real conversations about relationships, communication, marriage, dating, parenting, growth, and everything in between.
Through personal stories, debates, and lessons learned, Kareem and Shannon explore the moments that can bring couples closer or create unnecessary tension. From petty disagreements and communication breakdowns to love, accountability, and personal growth, each episode offers humor, honesty, and practical takeaways. However, this is not advice!

title: The Sausha Davis Show
author: Sausha Davis
description:
I’m Sausha Davis. Life and business mentor, writer, retreat host, mom of four, and horsewoman living on a ranch in Southern Oregon.


The Sausha Davis Show is where I talk about what I’m learning, what I’m questioning, and what I’ve already learned the hard way.


Self-trust, business, horses, motherhood, money, relationships, and what it actually looks like to build a life that feels like yours.


I spent years in sales and marketing before realizing I was more interested in the person making the decisions than the strategy itself.


There are no perfectly packaged lessons here. I hit record and talk. Sometimes my kids are yelling. Sometimes I change my mind. Sometimes the lesson comes from a horse.


I’m mostly making this for a younger version of me who thought everyone else knew something she didn’t.


If that sounds familiar, this show is for you.

title: Locked On Ole Miss Hit - Quick Takes on Ole Miss Rebels Football & Basketball
author: Locked On Podcast Network
description: Your daily hit of Ole Miss Rebels Football & Basketball covering news, trade rumors, game reactions, and sharp takes on everything happening with your team, all in five minutes or less. Done before your coffee is. New hits drop throughout the day, every day, all year long. Your Team. Every Day.
